# Accumulation buffer -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** Let cartons pile up behind the blade stop on a belt that never stops, then release a batch. Time the release by encoder pulses rather than by seconds: the pot is a release window in pulses, which is a distance.

**Done when.** Nothing gets past a raised blade while the belt keeps running, and the same pulse window releases the same amount of product at any drive speed — turn buffer.speed up and the release takes half as long and lets out the same number. A timer would have let out twice as many. The mushroom (panel.estop, normally closed) stops the buffer's drive and the outfeed within 200 ms and its trip latches: releasing it restarts nothing, and neither does Start or Reset alone -- only Reset, then Start.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`accumulation_buffer.st`](accumulation_buffer.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Accumulation buffer" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/accumulation_buffer.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   In the folder FactoryForge was extracted to:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   On Linux it is `./factoryforge-sidecar`. If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add
   `-o host <the address it reaches this machine on>` and read the warning
   it prints. Check the address map it prints against the table below.

   <!-- from-source -->
   (From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`
   in `sidecar/`, in place of the command above.)
   <!-- /from-source -->
3. Compile `accumulation_buffer.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh accumulation_buffer.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 10 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 10 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 10 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 4 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses. Stop the sidecar (Ctrl+C) first,
   then start the grader in one terminal:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar grade --scene accumulation-buffer
   ```

   and, in a second terminal, the sidecar with the bus port the grader
   printed:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

   (`./factoryforge-sidecar` on Linux, in both.)

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `buffer.actual` | PLC reads | float | 3x0 + 3x1 | `BufferActualHi` %IW100 + `BufferActualLo` %IW101 -> `BufferActual` : REAL | actual speed, % -- lags the reference while the drive ramps |  |
| `buffer.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `BufferFault` %IX100.0 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn |  |
| `buffer.run` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `BufferRun` %QX100.0 | run the drive | yes |
| `buffer.speed` | PLC writes | float | 4x0 + 4x1 | `BufferSpeedHi` %QW100 + `BufferSpeedLo` %QW101 -> `BufferSpeed` : REAL | speed reference, 0..100 % of 0.5 m/s; the drive ramps towards it | yes |
| `count_display.value` | PLC writes | int | 4x2 + 4x3 | `CountDisplayValueHi` %QW102 + `CountDisplayValueLo` %QW103 -> `CountDisplayValue` : DINT | number shown on the display () | yes |
| `emitter.emit` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `EmitterEmit` %QX100.1 | rising edge = feed one carton; hold each level well over one poll |  |
| `enc.count` | PLC reads | int | 3x2 + 3x3 | `EncCountHi` %IW102 + `EncCountLo` %IW103 -> `EncCount` : DINT | measuring wheel pulses, 100 per metre of belt travel | yes |
| `enc.rate` | PLC reads | float | 3x4 + 3x5 | `EncRateHi` %IW104 + `EncRateLo` %IW105 -> `EncRate` : REAL | pulse rate, pulses/s |  |
| `enc.reset` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `EncReset` %QX100.2 | a LEVEL: held TRUE keeps the count at zero | yes |
| `exit_eye.detect` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `ExitEyeDetect` %IX100.1 | TRUE while a carton is in the beam | yes |
| `outfeed.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `OutfeedFault` %IX100.2 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; a faulted drive does not turn, whatever it is told |  |
| `outfeed.rotate` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `OutfeedRotate` %QX100.3 | run the belt | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.3 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.4 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `PanelRed` %QX100.5 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `PanelReset` %IX100.4 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x6 + 3x7 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW106 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW107 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 40..300 p (starts at 120) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `PanelStart` %IX100.5 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x6 | `PanelStop` %IX100.6 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `released.count` | PLC reads | int | 3x8 + 3x9 | `ReleasedCountHi` %IW108 + `ReleasedCountLo` %IW109 -> `ReleasedCount` : DINT | cartons this remover has taken off the line, running total | yes |
| `stop.down` | PLC reads | bit | 1x7 | `StopDown` %IX100.7 | blade fully down | yes |
| `stop.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x8 | `StopFault` %IX101.0 | drive fault: TRUE = faulted; the blade stays where it is |  |
| `stop.raise` | PLC writes | bit | 0x6 | `StopRaise` %QX100.6 | raise the blade into the lane (holds cartons on a running belt) | yes |
| `stop.up` | PLC reads | bit | 1x9 | `StopUp` %IX101.1 | blade fully up | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x7 | `TowerGreen` %QX100.7 | tower lamp, green |  |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x8 | `TowerRed` %QX101.0 | tower lamp, red |  |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | bit | 0x9 | `TowerYellow` %QX101.1 | tower lamp, yellow |  |

## Four things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 7:
  `buffer.actual`, `buffer.speed`, `count_display.value`, `enc.count`,
  `enc.rate`, `panel.setpoint`, `released.count`. The program's first and last
  sections move them between the registers and plain DINT/REAL variables, so
  your logic never sees a register. OpenPLC's `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the
  *number* (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0, not 1.0), so the starter
  rebuilds a REAL bit by bit instead.
  [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh) compiles the helpers with
  OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button click in the 3D scene holds its tag for 0.2 s (the
  panel's Press Hold setting) and then leaves it off for at least as long, so
  every click is read several times: act on its rising edge, not its level.
  The grader holds each press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an
  output you want the scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
- **Every input reads FALSE until OpenPLC's first poll returns.** The runtime
  starts scanning before its Modbus master has read the slave, and
  `panel.estop` is normally closed, so for those first scans it looks struck.
  A trip latched on `NOT PanelEstop` then trips itself every time OpenPLC
  starts, and Start does nothing. Arm the trip only once the E-stop has read
  healthy (`IF PanelEstop THEN EstopSeen := TRUE; END_IF;` and trip on
  `EstopSeen AND NOT PanelEstop`), and keep refusing Start while it reads
  FALSE, so a cut wire still stops the line. The section 2 comment in the
  `.st` has the pattern;
  [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md#troubleshooting) says why.
